issues.legal_issue: At the stage of taking cognizance and issuing process, the court determines whether the complaint makes out a prima facie offence and does not assess whether the evidence will lead to conviction.
material_facts: The complaint alleged that the accused forged and prepared false documents on which a development agreement was based.
After the complaint was referred for investigation, the Trial Court recorded a sworn statement and issued process against the accused.
The High Court set aside the process after accepting that the dispute was civil in nature and considering the disputed document and the parties’ contentions.
issues.conclusion: The High Court should not have set aside the process by evaluating the merits at the threshold; the allegations had to be tested at trial, and the appeal was allowed.
issues.legal_principle: At the stage of taking cognizance and summoning, the court asks whether a prima facie case is made out and must not decide whether the material will lead to conviction. Defences and matters that may lead to acquittal at trial are not grounds for quashing at the threshold. The judgment relies on Sonu Gupta v. Deepak Gupta, (2015) 3 SCC 424.

predicates.process_challenge_in_criminal_complaint: The challenged decision concerns process issued against an accused in a criminal complaint.
predicates.complaint_discloses_offence_elements: The complainant's allegations, considered with the sworn statement, set out facts that prima facie disclose an offence.
predicates.merits_require_trial: The correctness of the allegations or the effect of the evidence depends on matters to be determined at trial.
predicates.process_is_not_set_aside_at_the_threshol: The process issued against the accused is not set aside at the threshold.

issues.definition: When a challenge concerns process in a criminal complaint, the complaint discloses offence elements, and the merits require trial, the process is not set aside at the threshold.

issues.legal_issue: A criminal complaint cannot be quashed solely because the dispute appears civil in nature when its allegations prima facie disclose the ingredients of an offence.
material_facts: The complainant alleged that the accused forged and prepared false documents to bring about a development agreement.
The High Court accepted the accused's contention that the dispute was entirely civil and quashed the criminal process.
The Supreme Court found that the complaint prima facie disclosed the alleged offences and held that their truth had to be decided at trial.
issues.conclusion: The criminal proceedings could not be interdicted merely because the allegations appeared civil in nature; the appeal was allowed and the High Court's judgment was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Quashing is appropriate where a complaint discloses no offence or is frivolous, vexatious, or oppressive, and the High Court may quash when the alleged facts do not constitute the offence. But a civil character to the dispute alone does not justify quashing if the complaint prima facie discloses the offence's ingredients. The judgment relies on Sonu Gupta v. Deepak Gupta, (2015) 3 SCC 424.

predicates.quashing_challenge_in_criminal_complaint: A party seeks to quash criminal proceedings initiated by a complaint.
predicates.complaint_discloses_offence_elements: The complainant's allegations, considered with the sworn statement, set out facts that prima facie disclose an offence.
predicates.dispute_appears_civil: The dispute also appears to concern civil rights or obligations.
predicates.criminal_proceeding_is_not_quashed_solel: The criminal proceeding is not quashed solely because the dispute appears civil.

issues.definition: When a quashing challenge concerns a criminal complaint whose allegations disclose offence elements despite the dispute appearing civil, the proceeding is not quashed solely as civil.
